title: Vampires and the Mongol rise
summary: How the Mongol conquest caught the undead off guard.

claims.text: To ancient vampires the whole Mongol era passes in a blink, yet in that moment empires fall and a small tribe of steppe nomads conquers the world.
Elders and ancestors alike are taken by surprise, all the more because the nomads are so ill-suited to vampiric control.
Kings and emperors in Europe and China rule from fixed cities and castles, open to influence and surrounded by courtiers to feed on; the steppe offers no such easy hold.

title: The Black Tortoise Court
summary: Wan Kuei of the northern steppe, the Demons of Xia.

claims.text: On the steppe, the hunting Cathayans are of the Black Tortoise Court, called the Demons of Xia by the Anda, who count them as ancient, unyielding enemies.
Like the Anda they ride among the nomads, above all the Tatars and Ongguts, but most of the court lives in the more crowded Jin Empire and Xixia Kingdom.
The Wan Kuei claim the Asian night as their own and have little love for displaced western blood-drinkers.

title: The Anda
summary: Cainite orphans of the Mongol steppe.

claims.text: The Anda and Wu Zao are the scattered orphans of Caine on the Mongolian steppe.
The Anda feel bound to the loose earth of the steppe, which they see as the body of Itugen, the Mother Goddess who shields them from the sun.
Tugen’s Embrace (Animalism 1, Protean 3) works like burial in the earth but lets the vampire take others along for extra blood, most often a rider’s horses.

title: The Road of the Yasa
summary: The barbarians’ Road of the steppe.

claims.text: Part Road of the Beast and part Road of Chivalry, the Road of the Yasa also holds ideas found in neither.
Its creed holds that settled city folk who cannot defend their lives and goods deserve to lose both; its followers wear the name Barbarians with pride.
Barbarians fiercely protect their mortal and Cainite families and their anda brothers, Embraced or not, and value personal honour, honesty and discipline.

title: Temujin after death
summary: Rumours that the Great Khan returned as a Wan Kuei.

claims.text: Unlike western vampires, a Wan Kuei is not brought over by another; only one brutal enough to fight free of hell returns, needing great will and great cruelty.
Within a year of the Great Khan’s death, rumours spread that Temujin has come back from Yomi as a Wan Kuei; they persist for over a century but are never confirmed.
One vampire claims before the Black Tortoise Ancestor to be Temujin, despite looking little like the khan.
Cainites on the steppe may have no choice but to feed from animals when no people are near, which serves between herds but harms them over time.
Animal blood is poor nourishment and gives fewer blood points than its size suggests.
Wan Kuei cannot feed from animals at all and starve long before any other problem arises.
